g.text: NeuralForecast model argument: the length of history in each training window.

text.style: fill: #222222; font: 7.8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: What it does: Each training example is input_size past weeks followed by the next h weeks to predict. The network only ever sees

text.style: fill: #222222; font: 7.8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: that window, so anything longer than it (a yearly peak, last year's holiday) is invisible.

text.style: fill: #222222; font: italic 7.8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: Why it matters here: Weekly retail demand repeats yearly. A 13-week window can't see last year, so the model falls back to the

text.style: fill: #222222; font: italic 7.8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: What moved: With input_size = 13, these got worse: fit to the training history, week-to-week tracking and how much the forecast

text.style: fill: #222222; font: 7.8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: moves, which went flatter (WAPE +1.30). Trade-off: bias moved from -2.3% to -3.6% with the fix (|bias| 1.4pt larger).

text.style: fill: #222222; font: 700 7.8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: Try on your data: Start at one season (52 weekly, 12 monthly) or two, and shorten only if you have evidence.

text.style: fill: #111111; font: 700 13.5px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: Show the model a full year: WAPE 46.6 → 45.3

text.style: fill: #555555; font: 8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: N-HiTS, Huber δ5 loss, 30,490 M5 weekly series, single seed. Only this setting differs between the two columns.

text.style: fill: #555555; font: 8px 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: Black = actuals; colored = 13-week forecasts from 3 origins (one fit at the first origin). Numbers cover all series.
